st: Put the soaked chickpeas, pork ribs and beef shank in a large pot with [[16 cups]] cold water.
Bring to a boil, then skim off the grey foam from the top for the first few minutes.
Reduce the heat to low, cover partly, and simmer for 60 minutes.
Add the chicken thighs, carrots, leek, [[2 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper. Simmer for another 30 minutes.
Add the potatoes and cabbage wedges and simmer 30 minutes more, until the chickpeas and potatoes are soft.
Lift out the meat and vegetables onto a warm platter. Check that the chicken is cooked through to 165°F (74°C).
Strain the broth into a clean pot and bring it to a boil. Add [[1 cup]] pasta shells.
Cook the pasta for 10 minutes until tender, then taste and add more salt if needed.
Serve the broth with pasta first as a soup, then serve the meat and vegetables as the second course.
Bring [[8 cups]] water to a boil with [[1 tsp]] salt. Add the potatoes and cabbage.
Boil for 20 minutes, until the potatoes are very soft.
Drain well and let the vegetables steam dry in the colander for 5 minutes.
Mash the potatoes and cabbage together with a fork or masher. Leave a little texture, and add [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the bacon for 6 minutes until crisp, then remove it and keep the fat in the pan.
Add the garlic to the bacon fat and cook for 30 seconds, then stir it into the mash with the bacon.
Add [[2 tbsp]] olive oil to the skillet over medium-high heat. Press the mash into the pan as a thick round cake.
Cook for 8 minutes until the bottom is deeply golden and crusty.
Slide the cake onto a plate, flip it back into the pan, and cook the other side for 6 minutes.
Cut into wedges and serve hot.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Boil the pasta tubes in salted water for 6 minutes, drain, and lay them on a tray so they do not stick.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the ground pork and chicken. Cook for 10 minutes, breaking up the meat, until no pink remains and it reaches 160°F (71°C).
Season with [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.25 tsp]] pepper. Let the filling cool for 10 minutes, then chop it finely.
Melt [[4 tbsp]] butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in [[0.25 cup]] flour and cook for 1 minute.
Slowly whisk in [[3 cups]] milk. Simmer, stirring, for 8 minutes until thick, then add [[1 tsp]] salt, [[0.25 tsp]] pepper and nutmeg.
Mix [[0.5 cup]] of the white sauce into the meat filling.
Spoon filling into each pasta tube and roll it closed. Place the tubes seam side down in a baking dish.
Pour the remaining sauce over the top and sprinkle with [[0.5 cup]] cheese. Bake for 25 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Rest 5 minutes, then serve.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Whisk the flour, [[0.5 cup]] sugar, [[2 tsp]] baking powder and [[0.25 tsp]] salt in a large bowl.
In a second bowl, whisk the eggs, [[0.25 cup]] olive oil, [[0.5 cup]] milk and [[1 tsp]] lemon zest.
Pour the wet mix into the dry and stir until a soft dough forms.
Knead the dough on a floured counter for 2 minutes, then let it rest for 10 minutes.
Roll the dough into a flat oval about 0.5 inch thick and move it to the baking sheet.
Brush the top with a little beaten egg or oil, then scatter [[0.25 cup]] pine nuts and a spoonful of sugar over it.
Bake for 25 minutes until golden brown.
Cool on a rack for 15 minutes, then cut into pieces.
Put [[1.75 cups]] of the milk in a saucepan with the lemon peel and cinnamon stick. Heat gently until steaming, then turn off the heat and let it sit for 15 minutes.
Whisk the remaining [[0.25 cup]] milk with the [[2 tbsp]] cornstarch until smooth.
In a bowl, whisk the egg yolks with [[0.5 cup]] sugar until pale and thick.
Whisk the cornstarch mix into the yolks. Remove the lemon peel and cinnamon from the milk.
Slowly pour the warm milk into the yolks while whisking constantly.
Pour everything back into the saucepan and cook over medium-low heat, stirring without stopping, for 6 minutes until it thickens like pudding. Do not let it boil hard.
Divide the custard among six shallow dishes.
Cool for 30 minutes, then cover and chill in the fridge for at least 4 hours.
Right before serving, sprinkle about [[1 tsp]] sugar over each custard in a thin even layer.
Caramelize the sugar with a kitchen torch until deep golden, or put it under a very hot broiler for 2 minutes. Let it harden for 2 minutes and serve.
